iut_type: End Product (Topre Corporation R4H keyboard), PTS report profile version consistency QA check
customer_question: (Internal report review, not a customer question:) Could you review this PTS test report before it's submitted for approval?
question_variants: Why must a profile report list only one declared version number rather than multiple?
What is the correct way to determine which version number a profile report should declare?
actual_issue: A submitted PTS test report for the BAS and DIS profiles listed inconsistent or incorrect version numbers, when each profile must have exactly one declared version, and that correct version is determined by the ICS information provided at the time PTS testing started -- requiring the report (and its underlying ICS) to be corrected before it could be approved and uploaded for customer delivery.
plain_english_explanation: Each Bluetooth profile referenced in a PTS report must declare exactly one version number -- in this case, BAS needed to be declared as version 1.0 and DIS as version 1.1. The authoritative source for which version applies is the ICS information that was provided at the time PTS testing began, not an assumption or a default value, so the report (and the ICS embedded within it) needed to be corrected to reflect those exact version numbers before submission. After the correction, the reviewer also noticed the revised BAS and DIS reports hadn't actually been uploaded to the shared Teams folder used for internal approval (only the HIDS and HOGP PTS reports were present), requiring a follow-up upload before the internal QA reviewer (Tanaka-san) could complete the approval step.
consultant_answer: Please correct the Profile version listed for BAS and DIS in this report -- each profile must have exactly one declared version, and per the ICS provided when PTS testing started, that should be BAS 1.0 and DIS 1.1. Please correct the ICS in the report as well, then make sure the revised BAS and DIS reports are actually uploaded to the shared folder (I only see HIDS and HOGP there currently) before asking Tanaka-san to approve.
decision_logic: When reviewing a PTS test report, verify that each referenced profile declares exactly one version number, and that this version matches the ICS information provided at the actual start of PTS testing -- not an assumed or default value -- before approving the report for delivery.
final_recommendation: Build profile version consistency (one declared version per profile, matching the ICS at test start) into the standard PTS report review checklist, and confirm that all revised reports referenced in a review conversation have actually been uploaded to the shared approval location before requesting sign-off from the internal QA reviewer.
risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting or approving a PTS report with an incorrect or inconsistent profile version declaration could result in registration evidence that doesn't match the product's actual ICS, potentially requiring correction after the fact or causing a registration discrepancy.
